review.material: Primary paper: shape operations and labels, formal grammar definition, square derivation and parametric extension.
review.limitations: The main definitions and worked examples were reviewed; no independent verification of every formal detail is implied. This uses the public teaching copy, not the unrelated local-only PDF.

sections.title: In brief
sections.text: A compact reference for what a shape grammar formally contains and how a rule acts. The paper connects geometric parts, labels, recursive derivation and parametric rule families.

sections.title: The question
sections.text: How can an algorithm be stated directly with drawings while precisely specifying matching, replacement and which outputs belong to its language?

sections.title: Main idea or claim
sections.text: A rule recognizes an embedded geometric part under a transformation and replaces it using the same transformation. Labels can direct this process without becoming permanent features of the final drawing.

sections.title: How the work approaches it
sections.text: Stiny defines shapes and operations, adds labelled points, specifies a grammar’s components, and derives a nested-square example. The parametric extension assigns coordinates under constraints to obtain a particular rule from a schema.

sections.title: Evidence and examples
sections.text: In the square example, a marker identifies the square to elaborate. One rule inscribes another square and moves the marker; another removes the marker to produce an unlabelled language member.

sections.title: What comes out of it
sections.text: The formula C′ = (C − t(A)) + t(B) unifies erasing and adding. Parametric grammars extend variation beyond a shape’s location, orientation and scale to permitted changes in its proportions or geometry.

sections.title: Limits to keep in mind
sections.text: This is a definitional introduction, not an efficiency or usability study. Its general transformation possibilities exceed this app’s finite search menu. Parameter assignment and geometric placement are distinct operations.

sections.title: What to take from it
sections.text: Track three things separately: the pattern being recognized, its transformation, and the rule’s replacement. Ask whether a visible label is a construction control or a desired final feature.
